title: Chapter 46 — The Property Manager
intro: The volume buyer — unit turns, the standard-unit program, and frictionless portfolio service.

sections.title: The Property Manager Mindset
sections.content:
Property managers are volume buyers with simple requirements. They do not care about CrystalDry technology or InstaView. They care about four things: price, reliability, speed of replacement, and minimizing tenant complaints.

They need reliable, affordable appliances that can be replaced quickly when they fail. They need consistent pricing across their portfolio — no re-quoting every time a unit needs a fridge. They need delivery coordinated with tenant schedules — not during work hours when nobody is home. And they need warranty service handled without involving the tenant more than necessary.

This is not a design conversation. This is a logistics and value conversation. Speak their language: cost per unit, turnaround time, portfolio pricing, tenant coordination.

sections.title: The Standard Unit Program
sections.content:
Create a standard appliance package at two or three price tiers. Budget tier for basic units — Amana, Hotpoint, Crosley. Mid-range for upgraded properties — Whirlpool, GE, Frigidaire. Premium for luxury rentals — Bosch, KitchenAid.

Standardize the models so every unit in a building gets the same fridge, range, and dishwasher. This simplifies ordering, delivery, parts stocking, and service. When unit 4B needs a fridge, it is the same fridge as every other unit — no spec conversation needed.

Offer portfolio pricing — a flat discount for the annual volume commitment. Even 5-8 percent off on a 50-unit annual volume is meaningful for the property manager. And the consistent, predictable revenue is valuable for you. Lock it in with a simple annual agreement.

sections.title: Frictionless Service
sections.content:
Property managers hate friction. Every phone call, every email back-and-forth, every coordination step is friction they do not want.

Create a reorder system where they can text you 'unit 4B needs a fridge, same as last time' and you handle everything — quote, order, delivery scheduling with the tenant, haul-away, and installation. One text from them. One confirmation from you. Done.

The property manager who has to call three times to get a fridge replaced will find someone easier to work with. The one who sends a text and gets a confirmation back in an hour will never leave.

For large portfolios, create a shared spreadsheet or simple portal showing every unit, what appliance is installed, the installation date, and the warranty expiration. This becomes your tool for proactive replacement recommendations — 'You have 12 dishwashers approaching 10 years. Want me to phase replacements over the next two quarters instead of waiting for them to fail?'
